newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines convicts German for mail-order brides.
newsitem.headline: Philippines convicts German for mail-order brides.

text.p: A Philippine court on Wednesday sentenced a German national to seven years in jail for advertising Filipina women for marriage in the West.
"I will not accept this," Bernhard Lauks, 48, said after judge Edgardo de los Santos issued his ruling in a trial held at the Bacolod regional court on central Negros island.

Lauks was accused of arranging mail-order marriages between Filipinas and Germans between 1990 and 1993. The Philippines has a specific anti-Mail Order Bride law, under which the maximum punishment is eight years imprisonment.
The judge said in his decision many Filipinas had been lured to marry foreigners by false promises of a better life abroad.
"It has become an almost acceptable proposition that poverty is the Siamese twin of prostitution, exploitation of women and children and other forms of crime," the judge said.
